A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OTora research and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–K. No material gaps prevent comparison; the appendix pages match in both text and rendered appearance.

before.justification: v1 reports original trigger-optimization and slowdown experiments, ablations, and appendix evaluations of costs, defenses, and transferability, including Tables 1–17.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including attack success, latency, reasoning-token inflation, task accuracy, and defense and transfer evaluations.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and Sections 3.3–3.4 retain the same insertion scoring, dynamic target co-evolution, trigger optimization, persistent payload design, and ICL-guided genetic search. No method component or objective changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use WebShop and InjecAgent-derived Email/OS tasks, with the same instruction/environment injection and transfer scenarios. No dataset, task, or evaluated environment is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: SNES, AutoDAN, and PAL in Table 1; GCG, I-GCG, and UDora in Table 2; and the same OVERTHINK-derived payload variants in Table 3. Appendix comparisons also retain their comparators.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendices D–K retain the same model configurations, optimization budgets, evaluation procedures, metrics, and success criteria, including the stated N=50 task instances per setting.

E4.justification: The insertion and scoring ablations in Section 5 and Appendices E–F, defense evaluations in Appendix I, and transfer analyses in Appendices G and J are unchanged. None is newly introduced in v3.

E5.justification: Both already report three-seed payload evaluation, cross-seed variance in Table 10, transfer averages with variability in Table 15, and 95% bootstrap accuracy intervals using 1000 resamples in Table 17. Reporting practices and run information are unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–17 and Figure 2 retain their results. For example, Table 3 reports the same LLaMA-70B/WebShop OTora-Persistent values in both: 325 s delay, 9.7× RTI, 92% Hit, and 96.1% accuracy. No result entries or findings change.

T1.justification: The threat-model assumptions, mathematical definitions, optimization objectives in Equations (1)–(4), and cost formulations in Equations (5)–(6) are unchanged. No theorem, proof, or derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same novelty claim for a unified two-stage R-DoS framework and the same claims of substantial slowdown with largely preserved task correctness. Their scientific scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: Interpretations of persistent reasoning overhead, transferability, and agent susceptibility remain unchanged. Appendices A–C and I retain the same mechanism explanations, applicability qualifications, and availability–correctness trade-offs.

D1.justification: The code-access statement, optimizer settings, hardware disclosure, token-pricing assumptions, cost breakdowns, and evaluation details are retained. The added author affiliations do not change technical or reproducibility information.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to UDora, OVERTHINK, and other prior research are unchanged. Bibliography edits correct typography and redundant wording without adding, removing, or replacing a cited work.

P1.justification: v3 adds Eindhoven and Macau affiliations, updates dates, standardizes instances of R-Dos to R-DoS, and makes small bibliography corrections. The scientific prose and section organization remain unchanged apart from text reflow.

P2.justification: Expanded front matter changes some main-text column and page breaks, with small spacing adjustments. Figure 1's caption and Algorithm 1's heading correct R-Dos capitalization. Figures, table structures, and appendix layouts otherwise remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 provides slight cosmetic polish through affiliation updates and typographic corrections. The methods, results, explanations, reproducibility information, and complete appendices are retained, leaving no meaningful net difference in scientific support or overall paper quality.
